title: Choose the visual world for Certificates
question: The roll assigned the Circulation Desk. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Circulation Desk
options.lineage: Library circulation: date-due cards, book pockets, and violet rubber stamps
options.thesis: Every certificate is a card with its dates stamped on it, and revoking one stamps it WITHDRAWN.
materials: ruled index-card stock with a red header rule
manila book pocket for one-time secrets
options.viewport: The inventory is the circulation ledger: one bar of counts stamped across the top (active, due within 30 days, withdrawn, CA valid until), then ruled rows with each expiry stamped in violet. The Enroll button is the one filled stamp.
options.risk: Can read as a nostalgic costume if the stamps decorate. It works only if every stamp is a real date or state.

raised.raise: Serials, fingerprints, and dates are set as full-length tabular monospace columns, never truncated to look tidy.
States are printed marks with no corner radius: a hairline at rest, filled when pressed, struck through when spent.
Violet belongs only to validity dates and the one live task, and red belongs only to revocation.
Each screen has one dominant object: the ledger, the enroll slip, or the CA authority card. Reference values sit in a drawer below.

options.label: Breaker Panel Directory
options.lineage: The house electrical panel and its handwritten circuit directory
options.thesis: Every certificate is a labelled circuit in the house panel, and revoking one throws its breaker.
materials: directory card in the panel door
options.viewport: A two-column panel schedule of certificates with toggle-state glyphs and a main-breaker block for the CA at the top.
options.risk: Industrial control-panel styling is close to where homelab dashboards already land, so it is the familiar choice.

options.label: Centre-rail reference setting
options.lineage: Wide-margin editions laid out with a ruling engine
options.thesis: Two short columns around a central rail of keys, with the apparatus hanging in the margin.
options.viewport: Certificate facts in twin columns around a rail of status keys.
options.case: Loses on both axes: admins don't recognise a scholarly edition, and the rail hides the table they scan.
options.kept: States as printed marks, with no radius anywhere.
options.risk: Reads as a book instead of a tool.

options.label: Datamatics field
options.thesis: Certificates as barcode columns in a strobing data field.
options.viewport: Serial numbers as a barcode wall.
options.case: Loses on both axes: strobing is hostile in an admin panel, and pure black and white cannot separate active, expired, and revoked.

options.label: Orienteering map
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering maps and course overprint
options.thesis: Fixed terrain colours, with the active course riding over them in purple.
options.viewport: Enrollment as a numbered course from control to control.
options.case: Loses on both axes: no admin thinks of a CA as terrain.
options.kept: One ink reserved for the active path.
options.risk: Map costume on a table app.

options.label: Zoo guide map
options.thesis: Swelling colour lobes divide the page.
options.case: Loses on both axes: playful overshoot undercuts the trust a CA needs.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Home Assistant-native admin: a top bar, stat tiles, rounded cards, and a data table, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Stat tiles across the top, a certificate table below, and an Enroll button at top right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other add-on panel by design.
